messages:
Elliot Price: Hey all — kicking off doc coordination for “Private observability minimum pack”. Need to lock doc ownership + info architecture this week so we can start drafting in Confluence. Main question: what lives in the *install guide* vs the *day-2 ops runbook* (and where do we put the troubleshooting tree)?

Elliot Price: Proposed IA (rough):
1) Install guide (VPC + on-prem): prereqs, supported components, helm/installer steps, validation checklist, common pitfalls.
2) Configuration reference: values.yaml / installer flags + defaults + toggles.
3) Day-2 ops runbook: troubleshooting, alert noise tuning, missing signals, escalation.

Elliot Price: Owners: I can take install guide, Kira takes runbook. Need SMEs for screenshots + real command outputs.

Talia Benson: +1 on splitting like that. From program side: we should make “Install guide” a linear path: prep → install → verify → handoff. Anything that smells like investigation should go to runbook.

Kira Thompson: Works for me. For runbook, I’d like a consistent structure per symptom (e.g. “Dashboards missing”, “Alerts not firing”, “Log drops”). If Support has their top 5 recurring issues, I’ll bake them in.

Markus Klein: From Pro Services POV, please keep install guide opinionated and short. Our customers get lost when it’s too many branches.

Markus Klein: Suggest install guide includes:
- A “Choose your mode” table (customer-managed Prometheus/Grafana vs Redwood-provided in-cluster) and what we support.
- Exactly one “happy path” command set.
- A required checklist we can use in go-live.

Sean Gallagher: +1. Also we should be explicit about what “supported” means from SRE: which alerts are paging by default vs informational. That belongs in runbook/alerting philosophy, but install guide should point to it.

Allison Grant: For IA: configuration reference needs to include the metrics/label contract requirements (high level) and cardinality gotchas. We’ve been bitten by docs that don’t warn folks not to add `request_id` as a label, etc.

Elliot Price: Good call. We can put detailed label/schema constraints in the “standards” page, but in config reference we’ll add a “do not do this” callout with examples.

Dev Patel: Support asks: can we please include screenshots of what “good” looks like? Right now tickets are like “latency seems high” and we’re missing a shared baseline.

Dev Patel: Specifically helpful:
- Gateway overview dashboard (RPS, p95/p99, 5xx)
- Runtime perf (prefill vs decode)
- GPU saturation
- “Install health” dashboard
And screenshots of the post-install validation output.

Owen Phillips: +1. If you can include one screenshot per dashboard with *where to look first* arrows/callouts, that reduces ping-pong. Also include the exact PromQL query for at least the “requests + errors + latency” panels so we can ask customers to run them quickly.

Bruno Silva: I can provide installer output + validation command examples once the CLI is stable. Right now the command is roughly:
`redwood-private observability install --pack-version X.Y.Z`
`redwood-private observability validate --format text`

Bruno Silva: Validation output will include checks like Grafana API reachability, Prometheus rule load status, and “required metrics present” probe. I’ll paste a sample once we merge PR-908.

Elliot Price: Perfect. Bruno, can you also grab an example of a failure mode? (e.g., Grafana RBAC deny or promtool parse error) so we can add a “common failure → fix” box.

Bruno Silva: Yep. We have a real one from staging last week (RBAC on provisioning SA). I’ll redact cluster names.

Kira Thompson: For screenshots: do we have a staging env with the dashboards already imported? If yes, I’ll take the “good state” screenshots. If not, I can use the wireframes but I’d prefer real Grafana.

Sean Gallagher: We have staging load-test results; Sergio can probably import dashboards and set time range to a noisy window so screenshots look realistic. I can coordinate.

Allison Grant: Please make sure screenshots don’t show tenant IDs or customer-like names. Use `tenant=example` or internal staging names.

Talia Benson: Action items (so we don’t lose this):
- Elliot: draft IA in Confluence + outline install guide sections
- Kira: propose runbook template (symptom → checks → likely causes → fixes → escalation)
- Bruno: provide sample `install` + `validate` output (success + RBAC failure)
- Sean: help source realistic dashboard screenshots from staging
- Dev/Owen: send top 5 Support issues for Private observability

Elliot Price: Great. Also question: where do we put “alert noise tuning workflow”? I’m leaning runbook with a link from install guide.

Sean Gallagher: Runbook. Install guide can have one line like “Expect alerts to fire during initial load; see noise tuning section.” But we don’t want operators tuning on day 0 without context.

Dev Patel: Agree, but please put a very short “if you’re getting paged immediately after install” checklist in install guide. That’s a real go-live scenario.

Kira Thompson: I can add a runbook section “First 24 hours after go-live” with:
- which alerts are expected to flap
- what to disable temporarily (if allowed)
- when to escalate

Elliot Price: Good compromise. Install guide: small “first-hour triage” box, with a link to full runbook.

Owen Phillips: Another recurring question: “Which components does Redwood support vs customer owns?” Can we add a table in install guide: responsibility matrix (Redwood vs Customer) for Prometheus, Grafana, log forwarder, storage, TLS certs.

Elliot Price: Yes. I’ll add a “Responsibility matrix” section in install guide, plus a “Supported backends” link.

Allison Grant: For config reference, I’ll send a snippet list of the default metric names/labels we’re relying on for dashboards so docs aren’t vague.

Bruno Silva: Re: screenshots of validation output — can include something like:
```
✓ Prometheus reachable: http://prometheus-operated:9090
✓ Rules loaded: 14 groups / 128 rules
✓ Required metrics present: redwood_gateway_requests_total, redwood_runtime_decode_seconds_bucket
✗ Grafana provisioning: permission denied (RBAC) on ConfigMap dashboards
  hint: ensure ServiceAccount redwood-grafana-provisioner has get/list on configmaps in namespace
```
I’ll confirm exact wording once we cut the release.

Elliot Price: That’s exactly what we need. Thanks.

Talia Benson: Timeline reminder: we need doc drafts ready for SRE/Sec review by end of next week to hit the hardening phase. Please keep screenshots optional-but-nice, not blocking.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: I’ll aim to deliver screenshots by Wed.

Dev Patel: I’ll DM Elliot/Kira with the Support issue list + links to relevant tickets.

Kira Thompson: Cool. Once I get that list, I’ll structure runbook around those. Also will add “escalation paths” (Support → SRE → Private Deployments) with who-to-page.

Elliot Price: Great. I’m creating the Confluence page tree now under Eng Private Deployments → Deployment Guides / Day-2 Ops. Will share links once created.

Elliot Price: (Last ask) If anyone has strong opinions on naming: “Minimum pack” vs “Baseline pack” vs “Observability pack” — please reply. I’m leaning “Private Observability Minimum Pack” to match the project.

Sean Gallagher: Keep “Minimum” for now; sets expectations.

Markus Klein: Agree — “Baseline” gets interpreted as “best practices”, and customers ask for more.

Elliot Price: Done. Thanks all.
